verdict.line: You lose if you stand in Ntofo Strikes range and let K'Sante stack into a Path Maker stun; you win by poking from Q range and punishing every cooldown he spends on Footwork.

brief.thesis: K'Sante carries the raw lane and solo-kill edge because his Q (Ntofo Strikes) stacks into a pull and his W (Path Maker) is a telegraphed stun-dash — both close distance Urgot's kit is built to punish, not invite. Urgot's 52.5% win rate over 872 games comes from refusing short trades, maxing E (Disdain) for the shield and knockback, and only extending once K'Sante's E (Footwork) or W is down.

theirWindow.when: Q at 2 stacks with E, W both up
theirWindow.what: This is his full engage kit live — the 2-stack shockwave pulls you into auto range, Footwork closes any remaining gap, and Path Maker's charge-up threatens a stun. Back off to Q range and do not feed him an auto to mark with Dauntless Instinct.

yourWindow.when: after he dashes with E or whiffs W
yourWindow.what: Footwork (10-8s cooldown) and Path Maker (14-10s cooldown) are his only ways to close distance — once either is spent he's stuck at melee range with no reset. Walk up and unload Q into W (Purge) while he has nothing to answer with.

start.why: Sustained damage and lane sustain for a matchup you win by trading from range over and over, not by one cooldown.

boots.why: K'Sante's passive (Dauntless Instinct) empowers his next auto after any ability lands — flat auto-attack reduction blunts that payoff.

core.why: Cooldown haste to keep Q/E online and armor shred that matters once he builds tank items
Tenacity and a damage-reduction shield vs his chain CC — Path Maker's stun into All Out's knockback
Scaling resistances for the extended, grindy fights this matchup turns into (59.1% win rate over 132 games, the most-played third item)

situational.when: you're ahead and want to close out the lane faster (60.8% win rate pick)
you need the extra mobility to catch or disengage K'Sante on open terrain
he's ahead and his All Out engage chains are landing clean — the active slow buys you the window to kite

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards the exact pattern this lane needs — landing consecutive ranged autos/Q hits from outside his engage range stacks the vulnerable debuff before he can close.

summoners.why: Highest measured win rate and pick rate (54%, 63.1% pick) — Ignite converts your poke lead into kill pressure once you force a trade under tower; Flash+Teleport (50.9%, 31.8% pick) is the alternative if you'd rather play for scaling and wave control.

playing.title: Poke at Q max range
playing.detail: Q (Corrosive Charge, 800 range) outranges both his Q (450) and W (600) — sit outside both and chip him down between his cooldowns.

playing.title: Respect the Path Maker charge-up
playing.detail: W telegraphs before it dashes, knocks back, and stuns — walk out of the line the moment you see the charge, don't wait to confirm direction.

playing.title: Never trade at 2 Q stacks
playing.detail: At 2 stacks of Ntofo Strikes his Q fires a shockwave that pulls you in — if you're already at 1 stack, disengage before he gets the second hit.

playing.title: Max E first for the shield
playing.detail: This build's E-first order (maxed by ~level 12-13) gives you the lowest Disdain cooldown and biggest shield, letting you tank through his all-in attempts instead of trading damage for damage.

playing.title: Punish a spent Footwork
playing.detail: Once his E is on cooldown (10-8s) he has no repositioning tool — step up and land W (Purge) plus autos while he's stuck in melee range.

playing.title: Hold R for the execute, not the engage
playing.detail: Fear Beyond Death's cooldown (100-70s) is too long to waste as a poke — fire it once he's already committed or low enough to threaten the execute.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and the win-rate figures above are measured from live games on the current patch (16.19.1); the matchup reasoning — why the trades favor you outside Q range and why his engage windows matter — is my own read on the kit.
